categories.name: Ransomware
categories.description: Malware that extorts victims, commonly by denying access to data or systems.

categories.name: Trojan
categories.description: Malware delivered or disguised as a program or file the victim expects or trusts.

categories.name: Remote-access trojan (RAT)
categories.description: A trojan that provides remote control or surveillance functionality.

categories.name: Spyware
categories.description: Software used to monitor or collect information about a user or system without appropriate consent.

categories.name: Keylogger
categories.description: Software or functionality that records keyboard input; legitimate accessibility and input tools can also observe input.

categories.name: Worm
categories.description: Malware capable of spreading between systems or removable media.

categories.name: Rootkit
categories.description: Techniques or software designed to conceal activity or maintain privileged access.

categories.name: Bootkit
categories.description: Malware that targets boot or pre-OS components to gain persistence or control.

categories.name: Information stealer
categories.description: Malware that collects information such as files, browser data, or credentials.

categories.name: Banking trojan
categories.description: A trojan that targets financial accounts, transactions, or banking credentials.

categories.name: Cryptominer
categories.description: Software that uses computing resources to mine cryptocurrency; legitimate miners exist.

categories.name: Adware
categories.description: Software that displays advertising; unwanted behavior depends on consent, disclosure, and persistence.

categories.name: Potentially unwanted application (PUA)
categories.description: Software whose installation or behavior may be unwanted, but which is not necessarily malware.

categories.name: Botnet malware
categories.description: Malware that compromises devices and coordinates them for operator-controlled activity, including distributed attacks.

categories.name: Modular malware framework
categories.description: Malware composed of loaders or modules whose capabilities can be extended or changed.

categories.name: Trojan / loader
categories.description: Malware that delivers, decrypts, or launches other components; delivery behavior alone does not identify the final payload.

capabilities.name: Keylogging
capabilities.meaning: Capturing keyboard input.
capabilities.whyMalwareUsesIt: May collect credentials, messages, or other typed information.
capabilities.legitimateUses: Accessibility, hotkey utilities, input method editors, remote support, and security testing.
safeIndicators: A passive process snapshot cannot establish keyboard capture; approved endpoint telemetry would be required.

capabilities.name: Screen capture
capabilities.meaning: Capturing screenshots or recording screen content.
capabilities.whyMalwareUsesIt: May observe user activity, credentials, or sensitive documents.
capabilities.legitimateUses: Screen sharing, conferencing, accessibility, recording, and support tools.
safeIndicators: A passive process snapshot cannot establish screen capture; approved endpoint telemetry would be required.

capabilities.name: Credential theft
capabilities.meaning: Accessing or collecting authentication secrets.
capabilities.whyMalwareUsesIt: Stolen secrets enable account takeover and further access.
capabilities.legitimateUses: Password managers, authentication brokers, backup, enterprise identity, and security software.
safeIndicators: No credential-store reads are monitored by this on-demand analyzer; do not infer this capability from a file path or process name.

capabilities.name: Browser-data theft
capabilities.meaning: Collecting browser profiles, history, saved data, or configuration.
capabilities.whyMalwareUsesIt: Browser profiles may contain valuable personal and account information.
capabilities.legitimateUses: Browser sync, backup, migration, accessibility, and endpoint security.
safeIndicators: A passive process snapshot cannot establish browser-data access; approved file-access telemetry would be required.

capabilities.name: Cookie/session theft
capabilities.meaning: Collecting session cookies or authentication tokens.
capabilities.whyMalwareUsesIt: A stolen session can permit account access without re-entering a password.
capabilities.legitimateUses: Browsers, password managers, identity providers, and authorized browser backup tools.
safeIndicators: No cookie or browser-database content is opened by this analyzer.

capabilities.name: File discovery
capabilities.meaning: Enumerating files, folders, or drives.
capabilities.whyMalwareUsesIt: May locate valuable data, credentials, or files to encrypt.
capabilities.legitimateUses: Search, indexing, backup, antivirus, synchronization, and file managers.
safeIndicators: A passive snapshot cannot distinguish ordinary enumeration from malicious discovery.

capabilities.name: System-information collection
capabilities.meaning: Reading operating-system, hardware, account, or environment information.
capabilities.whyMalwareUsesIt: May profile a target, select a payload, or fingerprint a victim.
capabilities.legitimateUses: Inventory, diagnostics, installers, compatibility checks, and device management.
safeIndicators: This app reports only its own read-only process and connection snapshot; it does not attribute general system queries to a process.

capabilities.name: Data collection
capabilities.meaning: Gathering user or system data for later processing or transfer.
capabilities.whyMalwareUsesIt: Collected data can be stolen, sold, or used for extortion.
capabilities.legitimateUses: Backup, search indexing, sync, analytics with consent, and endpoint security.
safeIndicators: A passive snapshot cannot identify the meaning or consent status of data handled by a process.

capabilities.name: Data exfiltration
capabilities.meaning: Sending collected data outside its intended boundary.
capabilities.whyMalwareUsesIt: Attackers may steal data for fraud, espionage, or extortion.
capabilities.legitimateUses: Cloud sync, backup, email, file transfer, and enterprise applications.
safeIndicators: An established TCP connection is observable, but payload content and intent are not inspected.

capabilities.name: Persistence
capabilities.meaning: Arranging for software to start again after logon, restart, or service startup.
capabilities.whyMalwareUsesIt: Maintains access after the initial execution or reboot.
capabilities.legitimateUses: Installed applications, device drivers, accessibility tools, and enterprise agents.
safeIndicators: Exact executable path referenced by a Run key, service ImagePath, or scheduled-task action.

capabilities.name: Startup modification
capabilities.meaning: Adding or changing an automatic logon/startup entry.
capabilities.whyMalwareUsesIt: Runs code again when a user signs in.
capabilities.legitimateUses: User-approved applications, update agents, and productivity utilities.
safeIndicators: An exact executable-path match in the current-user or machine Run/RunOnce registry keys.

capabilities.name: Scheduled-task persistence
capabilities.meaning: Using a scheduled task to start a program later or at logon.
capabilities.whyMalwareUsesIt: Provides repeat execution and can blend into routine task scheduling.
capabilities.legitimateUses: Windows maintenance, software updates, backups, and enterprise management.
safeIndicators: An exact executable-path match in a task action under the Windows Task Scheduler store; task triggers and authorization are not judged.

capabilities.name: Service-based persistence
capabilities.meaning: Registering an executable as a Windows service.
capabilities.whyMalwareUsesIt: Can provide unattended execution, including before user logon.
capabilities.legitimateUses: Drivers, security software, databases, device support, and server applications.
safeIndicators: An exact executable-path match in a Windows service ImagePath registry value.

capabilities.name: Process injection
capabilities.meaning: Executing code inside another process.
capabilities.whyMalwareUsesIt: May conceal execution or access another process's resources.
capabilities.legitimateUses: Debuggers, accessibility, security products, profilers, and compatibility tools.
safeIndicators: Process memory is not read and injection is not monitored by this on-demand analyzer.

capabilities.name: Suspicious process creation
capabilities.meaning: Creating child processes in a context that merits review.
capabilities.whyMalwareUsesIt: May launch scripts, transfer tools, or additional payloads.
capabilities.legitimateUses: Installers, browsers, development tools, shells, and update services.
safeIndicators: A point-in-time process list does not provide parent-child creation history.

capabilities.name: Command-and-control communication
capabilities.meaning: Communicating with infrastructure controlled by an operator.
capabilities.whyMalwareUsesIt: Enables remote commands, tasking, or stolen-data transfer.
capabilities.legitimateUses: Cloud services, remote support, games, messaging, and enterprise management.
safeIndicators: The analyzer can observe an established IPv4 TCP peer for a running process, but cannot determine command-and-control intent or reputation.

capabilities.name: Remote-access functionality
capabilities.meaning: Allowing another user or system to interact with the device remotely.
capabilities.whyMalwareUsesIt: Enables remote operation, surveillance, or unauthorized control.
capabilities.legitimateUses: Remote Desktop, support tools, administration, and conferencing.
safeIndicators: An active connection alone does not identify whether remote access is authorized.

capabilities.name: File encryption
capabilities.meaning: Encrypting files or data.
capabilities.whyMalwareUsesIt: Ransomware can deny access to victim data.
capabilities.legitimateUses: Ransomware protection, disk encryption, backup, privacy, and document security.
safeIndicators: Bulk file modifications are not watched in this snapshot; no file-content modification monitoring is enabled.

capabilities.name: File deletion
capabilities.meaning: Removing files or data.
capabilities.whyMalwareUsesIt: May destroy data, backups, or recovery options.
capabilities.legitimateUses: Cleanup, uninstallers, temporary-file removal, and synchronization.
safeIndicators: File deletion events are not monitored by this on-demand analyzer.

capabilities.name: Security-software interference
capabilities.meaning: Attempting to disable, bypass, or impair security controls.
capabilities.whyMalwareUsesIt: May reduce detection or block remediation.
capabilities.legitimateUses: Security-product installers and documented administrative configuration.
safeIndicators: This analyzer reads current Defender status through the existing integration; it does not attribute historical setting changes to a process.

capabilities.name: Registry modification
capabilities.meaning: Changing Windows or application registry data.
capabilities.whyMalwareUsesIt: May establish persistence, alter security settings, or change system behavior.
capabilities.legitimateUses: Windows settings, installers, device management, and normal application preferences.
safeIndicators: Current startup/service references can be inspected, but registry write history is not collected.

capabilities.name: Network discovery
capabilities.meaning: Finding hosts or services reachable on a network.
capabilities.whyMalwareUsesIt: May identify additional targets or valuable services.
capabilities.legitimateUses: Network inventory, troubleshooting, device discovery, and management.
safeIndicators: Network scanning behavior is not monitored; a current TCP connection does not prove discovery.

capabilities.name: Lateral movement
capabilities.meaning: Moving from one device or account to another.
capabilities.whyMalwareUsesIt: Expands access across an organization or home network.
capabilities.legitimateUses: Remote administration, deployment, and enterprise management.
safeIndicators: Cross-device activity is not observed by this local snapshot.

capabilities.name: Privilege escalation
capabilities.meaning: Obtaining permissions beyond those initially available.
capabilities.whyMalwareUsesIt: May enable system-wide changes or access to protected data.
capabilities.legitimateUses: Installers and administrators using standard Windows UAC elevation.
safeIndicators: The analyzer does not monitor token or privilege changes.

capabilities.name: Downloading additional components
capabilities.meaning: Fetching additional software or data from another location.
capabilities.whyMalwareUsesIt: Allows a small initial program to obtain later payloads or modules.
capabilities.legitimateUses: Application updates, installers, browsers, and package managers.
safeIndicators: A point-in-time network connection does not reveal downloaded content or origin.

capabilities.name: Executing additional components
capabilities.meaning: Starting another executable, script, or module.
capabilities.whyMalwareUsesIt: Separates delivery, persistence, and payload roles.
capabilities.legitimateUses: Installers, updaters, shells, and application plugin systems.
safeIndicators: Parent/child process history is not monitored by this on-demand analyzer.

capabilities.name: Cryptocurrency mining
capabilities.meaning: Using CPU/GPU resources to perform cryptocurrency proof-of-work.
capabilities.whyMalwareUsesIt: An operator may monetize unauthorized resource use.
capabilities.legitimateUses: Explicitly authorized research or user-selected mining software.
safeIndicators: No sustained resource telemetry or mining workload inspection is performed.

capabilities.name: User-writable execution location
capabilities.meaning: An executable resides in a commonly user-writable folder such as Downloads, Temp, or AppData.
capabilities.whyMalwareUsesIt: These locations can permit execution without installation or administrator rights.
capabilities.legitimateUses: Portable apps, development tools, self-updaters, and user-installed software.
safeIndicators: The selected file's canonical location is compared with the signed-in user's Temp, Downloads, and AppData folders; location alone is not suspicious proof.

capabilities.name: Unsigned or invalidly signed executable
capabilities.meaning: Windows Authenticode does not establish a valid trusted signature for a PE executable.
capabilities.whyMalwareUsesIt: Some malware is unsigned or uses an invalid signature.
capabilities.legitimateUses: Open-source tools, internal software, scripts, and older programs may be unsigned.
safeIndicators: Windows Authenticode verification result for the selected file; an unsigned file is not automatically malicious.

capabilities.name: Established IPv4 TCP connection
capabilities.meaning: A running process has an established IPv4 TCP connection to a non-loopback peer; this snapshot does not determine whether the peer initiated the connection.
capabilities.whyMalwareUsesIt: Malware may communicate with remote infrastructure or transfer data.
capabilities.legitimateUses: Most browsers, sync clients, games, conferencing, and update services.
safeIndicators: A point-in-time TCP owner-PID table is matched to the selected executable path; peer reputation, connection direction, and traffic content are not inspected.

capabilities.name: Botnet propagation
capabilities.meaning: Compromising reachable or vulnerable devices so they can be controlled as part of a botnet.
capabilities.whyMalwareUsesIt: A larger population of compromised devices increases reach and attacker-controlled resources.
capabilities.legitimateUses: Authorized device management and security research may inventory or administer device fleets.
safeIndicators: A local point-in-time file scan cannot observe remote device compromise or prove that a device joined a botnet.

capabilities.name: Distributed denial-of-service activity
capabilities.meaning: Coordinated traffic from multiple systems intended to disrupt a target service.
capabilities.whyMalwareUsesIt: Botnet operators may monetize disruption, extortion, or access to rented attack capacity.
capabilities.legitimateUses: Authorized load testing and resilience exercises require explicit scope and consent.
safeIndicators: This analyzer does not inspect traffic volume, packet contents, or remote targets and cannot detect DDoS activity.

capabilities.name: Weak device-credential abuse
capabilities.meaning: Attempting default or weak credentials against network-connected devices.
capabilities.whyMalwareUsesIt: Successful authentication can enable unauthorized device compromise and botnet recruitment.
capabilities.legitimateUses: Authorized device inventory and credential audits may test configurations under an approved scope.
safeIndicators: A local Windows file snapshot does not monitor authentication attempts against remote devices.

capabilities.name: Anti-analysis evasion
capabilities.meaning: Using checks or obfuscation intended to impede security analysis or automated inspection.
capabilities.whyMalwareUsesIt: It may delay analysis and reduce the effectiveness of automated detection.
capabilities.legitimateUses: Commercial software protection and anti-tamper systems can use similar techniques.
safeIndicators: This analyzer does not execute files or infer evasion from obfuscation; source-backed family metadata is context only.

capabilities.name: Modular payload loading
capabilities.meaning: Using separate loadable components to extend or change malware functionality.
capabilities.whyMalwareUsesIt: Operators can add capabilities after initial access and tailor components to a victim.
capabilities.legitimateUses: Plugin architectures, application extensions, and update systems also load modules.
safeIndicators: A read-only file scan does not establish which modules were loaded at runtime; family records describe published reporting only.

capabilities.name: Encrypted payload archive
capabilities.meaning: Storing or transporting components in an encrypted or custom archive.
capabilities.whyMalwareUsesIt: Encryption can conceal payload content from casual inspection and support staged delivery.
capabilities.legitimateUses: Installers, backups, and secure software distribution routinely encrypt archives.
safeIndicators: This analyzer does not unpack files or infer malicious intent from encrypted data.

capabilities.name: Long-term access support
capabilities.meaning: Maintaining or extending an operator's access after an initial compromise.
capabilities.whyMalwareUsesIt: Persistent access can enable later collection or follow-on operations.
capabilities.legitimateUses: Remote administration and enterprise agents provide persistent authorized access.
safeIndicators: A family-level report of long-term access is not observed behavior for a scanned file; no attribution follows from similarity.

capabilities.name: Victim communication or recovery infrastructure
capabilities.meaning: Infrastructure used to communicate extortion demands or provide victim negotiation/recovery interactions.
capabilities.whyMalwareUsesIt: Operators use communication channels to coordinate extortion and maintain victim contact.
capabilities.legitimateUses: Customer support and recovery services are legitimate in unrelated contexts.
safeIndicators: This analyzer does not inspect websites, messaging networks, or remote infrastructure.

detectionRules.name: Unsigned user-writable file with persistence and an established TCP connection
detectionRules.rationale: Four independent snapshot indicators are correlated. This is still suspicious activity, not proof of malware or attribution to a family.

detectionRules.name: Unsigned user-writable file with a persistence reference
detectionRules.rationale: Multiple independent indicators warrant review. Legitimate portable software and user-installed updaters can produce similar evidence.

detectionRules.name: Unsigned user-writable running file with an established TCP connection
detectionRules.rationale: The location, signature state, and connection are observable, but the peer's reputation and traffic intent are unknown.

families.name: WannaCry
families.description: MITRE ATT&CK documents WannaCry as ransomware associated with file encryption and worm-like spread. This record is descriptive threat intelligence, not a file signature.
typicalBehaviors: File encryption
Network propagation behavior documented by public incident reporting
persistenceMethods: Family-specific persistence details are not asserted by this compact record.

families.name: Emotet
families.description: MITRE ATT&CK describes Emotet as modular malware used as a downloader for other malware variants. Capability notes are family-level reporting and do not identify a particular file.
typicalBehaviors: Modular delivery and downloading of additional malware, as described by MITRE ATT&CK.
persistenceMethods: No family-specific persistence IOC is bundled.

families.name: TrickBot
families.description: MITRE ATT&CK documents TrickBot modules that search for files and collect browser history and cookies. The same broad data-access behaviors also occur in legitimate backup, browser, and security software.
typicalBehaviors: File discovery and browser-data collection are described in MITRE ATT&CK reporting.
persistenceMethods: No family-specific persistence IOC is bundled.

families.name: NanoCore
families.description: MITRE ATT&CK describes NanoCore as a modular remote access tool used to spy on victims and steal information.
typicalBehaviors: Remote access and surveillance capabilities are documented by MITRE ATT&CK.
persistenceMethods: No family-specific persistence IOC is bundled.

families.name: FinFisher
families.description: MITRE ATT&CK describes FinFisher as commercial surveillance spyware with anti-analysis techniques. Its dual-use context and targeted deployment require careful attribution.
typicalBehaviors: Surveillance and anti-analysis behavior are described in public research cited by MITRE ATT&CK.
persistenceMethods: No family-specific persistence IOC is bundled.

families.name: Conficker
families.description: MITRE ATT&CK describes Conficker as a Windows worm that used the MS08-067 vulnerability to spread.
typicalBehaviors: Worm-like spread targeting Windows systems is documented by MITRE ATT&CK.
persistenceMethods: No family-specific persistence IOC is bundled.

families.name: Dridex
families.description: MITRE ATT&CK documents Dridex as a banking Trojan. Family-level capability notes are not a detection verdict for an individual file.
typicalBehaviors: Financial credential targeting is described in the references cited by MITRE ATT&CK.
persistenceMethods: No family-specific persistence IOC is bundled.

families.name: Lumma Stealer
families.description: Windows information stealer offered through a malware-as-a-service model. Fraunhofer FKIE Malpedia reports targeting cryptocurrency wallets and 2FA browser extensions, collecting sensitive information, exfiltrating data, and a non-resident loader capable of delivering additional payloads. These are family-level capabilities, not observations about a scanned file.
typicalBehaviors: Targets cryptocurrency wallets and two-factor-authentication browser extensions
Exfiltrates collected data through HTTP POST in documented samples
Non-resident loader can deliver EXE, DLL, and PowerShell payloads
families.firstObservedTimeframe: Available through a malware-as-a-service model since at least August 2022.

families.name: PureRAT
families.description: Remote-access trojan used to remotely control a victim's PC. Netresec equates PureRAT with ResolverRAT and describes PureHVNC as its predecessor, not an alias. Documented capabilities include viewing and controlling the user interface, webcam/microphone access, keystroke recording, file transfer, and network proxying.
typicalBehaviors: Remote viewing and input control
Webcam and microphone access
File upload/download and traffic proxying

families.name: DarkTortilla
families.description: A configurable .NET-based crypter/loader reported delivering information stealers, RATs, and other payloads. Fraunhofer FKIE Malpedia describes add-on packages and anti-analysis/anti-tamper controls. Its profile says it may have been active since at least August 2015; this is a qualified estimate, not a confirmed first-seen date.
typicalBehaviors: Delivers additional malware and add-on packages
Uses anti-analysis and anti-tamper controls
families.firstObservedTimeframe: Possibly active since at least August 2015; qualified estimate in the cited profile.

families.name: CryptBot
families.description: Windows information stealer. Fraunhofer FKIE Malpedia describes theft of browser credentials, cryptocurrency-wallet data, cookies, and credit-card data, screenshot capture, and uploading collected data in a ZIP archive to command-and-control infrastructure.
typicalBehaviors: Collects browser and wallet data, cookies, and payment-card information
Captures screenshots
Bundles collected data for upload

families.name: XWorm
families.description: Fraunhofer FKIE Malpedia describes malware with a capability range from RAT to ransomware. A separately cited campaign analysis documents WMI execution, fileless loading, and a .NET persistence module in that campaign; campaign-specific observations are not treated as universal family behavior.
typicalBehaviors: RAT-to-ransomware capability range reported by Malpedia
WMI execution and .NET persistence were described in a specific LATAM campaign

families.name: Mirai
families.description: Self-propagating malware that compromises vulnerable IoT devices and forms botnets used in DDoS attacks. CISA reports scanning for vulnerable devices using common default credentials. The cited advisory does not establish a specific operating-system platform or a definitive first-seen date.
typicalBehaviors: Scans the Internet for vulnerable IoT devices
Uses a short list of common default usernames and passwords in the cited incidents
Compromised devices are used in botnet attacks
targetPlatforms: IoT devices; specific operating systems not identified in the cited advisory

families.name: Black Basta (Basta ransomware)
families.description: Ransomware-as-a-service variant using double extortion: encrypting systems and exfiltrating data. CISA/FBI/HHS/MS-ISAC report that it was first identified in April 2022. This entry treats the requested 'Basta' as Black Basta, as documented in the joint advisory.
typicalBehaviors: Encrypts systems and exfiltrates data
Ransom notes direct victims to a unique code and onion-site contact

families.name: NeedyMantis
families.description: Modular post-compromise malware framework. Microsoft describes multiple loaders, custom encrypted archives, a custom executable format, and modules that extend functionality and support maintaining long-term access. Microsoft traces observed activity to at least October 2025.
typicalBehaviors: Uses multiple loaders and encrypted component archives
Modules extend functionality after initial access
DLL sideloading and persistence were observed in analyzed activity

indicators.context: Microsoft-reported sample hash for WinSparkle.dll; sample-specific IOC, not a family-wide signature.

persistenceMethods: DLL sideloading observed in analyzed activity; persistence described in the Microsoft report.
families.firstObservedTimeframe: Activity dates back to at least October 2025.

families.name: DeadLock ransomware
families.description: Microsoft describes a Rust-based ransomware operation using double extortion and decentralized victim communication/data-leak infrastructure. First observed in July 2025. The cited report includes IOCs and Microsoft Defender detections, but no stable family-wide signature is asserted here.
typicalBehaviors: Encrypts victim files and threatens data publication
Uses decentralized communication and leak/recovery infrastructure
Analyzed Windows encryptor uses the .dlock suffix; this sample behavior is not a complete standalone detection rule

indicators.context: Microsoft-described extension used by analyzed DeadLock encryptor samples; not unique proof of infection.
Microsoft-described marker in analyzed samples; not treated as a standalone confirmed detection.

targetPlatforms: Windows encryptor described in the cited report
